It is a sentence like any other and it is licensed by that field exactly as every other sentence is licensed; it fires rarely, in a different shape each time, and no dossier block carries more than one (DA-6). (2) WHERE THE ENGINE HOLDS NO FIELD AT ALL — the world has not merely an empty value but no question — THE SLOT IS OMITTED, SILENTLY, and the omission is not itself announced. WHY TWO AND NOT ONE: ruling (4) gives every element its full FORM, and the owner's own qualification is decisive — full form is not full content, and a slot the world has no fact for is an honest absence rather than a manufactured detail. So the FORM is full — every element the world holds gets its entry, its slots and its typography, sized by the place's own rank and never by its importance in play — and the CONTENT of a slot is written, declared absent, or absent-and-unmentioned, in that order, according to what the engine actually holds. HELD: R5 slot-bearing share 0.032 must not rise as a side-effect — a crier that starts naming places to sound differentiated has broken its own construction (own row 40).
rules.faultGuard: Fault 13 (dialogue — one voice with swapped vocabulary; 14 documents) and, at pool level, fault 9 (each people's register as a fixed tic list — tolkien:C1 names this itself). GUARDS: W 20's 'a register is a syntax difference, not a word-list difference', with Gary K. Wolfe's negative case as the diagnostic (voices prohibited from developing their own); H 14's ordering — length and clause habit FIRST, vocabulary second, because a per-speaker word list applied as a lookup produces caricature on a metronome; M 25's — dropping letters to signal rank is a tell and an insult at once; T C1's — the mediating figure's RANGE is itself a characterising fact, so one voice must carry a wide range or the set is a lookup table.
rules.grammar: THE LICENSING FIELD IS MISSING TODAY AND THE RULE SAYS SO: VOICE_LINES is keyed by category × bucket and carries no speaker role. Under R-DST-B a role-keyed register may not be written where no typed office field exists — the rule constrains emission, it does not licence inventing a role. This is HP-6's law applied to voice.
obeys: (5) THE BRACKWATER LESSON — a voice differentiated by a role the data does not hold is a sentence buying an effect with a fact; the rule refuses to fire rather than manufacture the role.
(7) product scope — a role, never a NAMED character's fate; and the archivist never borrows a speaker's register (hobb:14's own boundary).
(1) allocate — six authors converge on one mechanism, which is why this is the register's load-bearing rule and not an average of six.
rules.test: Measure per-pool within-pool word sd and clause-count spread over newsVoice.js. The real test is the negative control: STRIP THE VOCABULARY from two role-differentiated pools and check whether a blind reader still separates them by syntax alone — the rename test (tolkien:C5, dnd:45, tolkien:I3's register-variance-across-speakers walker check). Acceptance U10 and U12 (R-DST-B is in no rule and four items breached it; a role asserted from a field that does not carry it is the same breach).

rules.statement: In the Herald, no sentence names what a fact means. Where a receipt carries a second sentence, that sentence carries a NEW FACT, and its kind varies — a condition, a prohibition, an absence, an object, a name not given. A 'That is / This is' tail carrying the pool's own discriminating claim is not a gloss and is not cut.
rules.figure: R3 gloss tail ', which' 0.034 — 8.5× the 0.004 median, PROBE_ALL §6's own outlier row — against ZERO which-tails in Martin's 12,422-word chronicle (B0.2) → DOWN to ≤0.010, a cut of 0.024 (~70%), NOT to zero, because A9 protects the tail carrying the pool key's discriminating claim and U9 proves the estate cut exactly that twice. Second: R3 2nd-sentence-summary rate 0.016, held at or below present. BOTH HALVES ARE R3 AND ARE DEFERRED TO HP-2's SIGNATURE; the rule binds R4b and R5 immediately, where the gloss rate is already 0.000 — a hold, not a cure.
rules.faultGuard: Fault 1 (the gloss, 14 documents) in its cruellest form (wolfe:15's own): the flat report, then one sentence telling the reader it was terrible. GUARDS: W 15's — the whole technique is the MISSING second sentence, and Beck's 'morally inconsistent' matters because perfectly even coldness is its own mannerism, so the rate is not zero; K 30's — 'always end on an object' is itself a fixed move, so the KIND of standing fact varies across a pool; T A5's — the short sentence is earned only when it carries new fact, never a verdict on the previous fact.
rules.grammar: A typed CLOSE move whose kind is drawn, seeded, from kay:30's five kinds. R-DST-B binds it: a receipt closing on a consequence needs the consequence RECORDED, not inferred — an event move only where an event-provenance field exists, and a standing configuration field licenses a structural clause and never a historical one.
obeys: (5) THE BRACKWATER LESSON directly — the kicker sentence asserting a fact the generator holds no data for is exactly what this bars; its positive form is that a second sentence must be a SECOND FACT, not a meaning.
(6) B-CLAIM — a claim may not be spent and a meaning may not be bought.
(3) the close is a seeded choice among five kinds, never one shape.
rules.test: The Herald arm's 2nd-sentence-summary and ', which' counters, plus kay:30's walkable question — does the last sentence assert a present condition? Acceptance U9 (the gloss test has no guard for the case where the gloss is the band's distinguishing claim; run the sibling-pool check BEFORE the cut fires) and U5 (a close-on-a-thing rule was cited eight times and delivered once — the walker must assert DELIVERY, never citation).

rules.statement: In the Herald, every office, exemption, count, actor and saying named in a line must come from a typed row the engine holds. Where the table has no row, the line is not written. A price may be named without a figure; an office may not be named without an office.
rules.figure: The exposure is R5's slot-bearing share 0.032 (PROBE_ALL §3; own row 40) — 12 of 373 crier lines carry a slot, so 361 assert on the crier's own authority — against R3's 0.578 (4.28× the median) and R4b's 0.500 (3.7×), where the slot machinery already does most of the licensing. DIRECTION: the count of un-slotted OFFICE / EXEMPTION / COUNT nouns in R5 → 0 unlicensed. SIZE: NOT MEASURED — the census is owed (open question 5). The rate 0.032 must NOT be moved by this rule: the cure is not to slot the crier (that breaks its settlement-agnostic construction) but to bar the unlicensed noun.
rules.faultGuard: Fault 24 (fabrication in the record, 15 documents STRONG), whose own constraint sentence is the whole rule (the finite-semantics law), with its named trap: HOLLOW SPECIFICITY — a precise-sounding particular the engine does not hold is the fault, not the cure. Plus fault 11 (the vague authority, 24 documents). GUARD AGAINST OVER-CORRECTION: wolfe:3's positive form — the concrete in a WORKING SENTENCE, never an inventory, and the price without the number (row 1028, named by its file the model for our no-digits rule); kay:11's — the four forms are a pool drawn with long gaps, never a checklist, and some entries fire none.
rules.grammar: This rule creates the register's licensing spine. Ruling (5) owes an INSTITUTION TABLE: typed rows for who holds office, who counts, who is exempt, what each institution does. Every PARTY, BILL and SAYING move is licensed by that table and nothing else. The BILL move is DOUBLE-licensed: event provenance AND an institution row.
obeys: (5) verbatim and centrally — the generator is a clerk, never a writer; no sentence may buy an effect with a fact. The Brackwater kicker fails this rule at the bailiff and again at the priest.
(7) FINITE SEMANTICS — typed buckets, the AI a clerk never a writer; and DEITY DOCTRINE, since a priest named by a Herald line is a culture's officer, never a theological claim.
(4) full FORM is not full CONTENT — the rule refuses the manufactured detail while leaving the form intact.
rules.test: The SAME-ENTRY CONTRADICTION WALKER ruling (5) owes: an entry's sentences checked against its own facts and against the pool's sibling variants. Negative control, executable by hand today: run it on the Brackwater line itself and require it to fire on the exemption clause about the priest and the counting clause about the bailiff. Acceptance U12 (R-DST-B is in no rule and four items breached it) and U11 (§0d's closed count and duration vocabularies are absent from every drafted rule; digit-free is not band-clean).

rules.statement: In the Herald, no line hedges a quantity, a strength or a likelihood. A provenance hedge — naming where a report came from — is licensed only inside the information family, never twice in one entry, and never on a belief.
rules.figure: R3 AI-tells/variant EXOGENOUS 0.004 (half the 0.008 median) and R4 0.000 — the Herald's receipt half is already the cleanest column in the estate on this axis, so the rule is a HOLD there. The exposure is R4b at 0.020 (2.5×) and R5 at 0.024 (3×, the corpus's highest). SIZE: R5 exogenous tells 0.024 → ≤0.008 (the median), which on 373 variants is 9 variants → ≤3; R4b 0.020 → ≤0.010, which on 50 variants is 1 variant → 0, and is therefore a ONE-ROW ACT rather than a distribution — the rule says so rather than dressing a single row as a rate.
rules.faultGuard: Fault 11 (the vague authority: 'it is said') in the over-hedging direction, and fault 19 in the over-correction direction — a copula purge to avoid a hedge produces machine-avoidance prose, refuted directly by dnd:9's in-house measurement (is/are 24.84 per thousand against was/were 0.65). GUARD: keep the plain copula; a hedge marks a SOURCE, never a quantity, and never twice in one entry (dnd:3's own rule). Note the honest deduction: dnd:3's archivist half rests on Alexander alone and does NOT count here; only the three-source no-hedge limb does.
rules.grammar: A prohibition on a modifier class, not a move. Its one licensed exception is a PLACEMENT rule: the provenance hedge lives in the R3 information family, which is the Wolfe fence's existing home (RULES Part B: truth prose never draws from the belief ledgers).
obeys: (6) B-CLAIM — a modality may not be spent, and a hedge added is a modality spent in the other direction.
(7) the deity doctrine, via wolfe:16 — a hedge never softens a belief, because a belief is a cultural fact and not a claim about the world.
(2) the no-hedge limb is taken at its own three sources and the archivist limb's single source is left where it belongs.
rules.test: A hedge-lexicon counter over the four Herald homes, split into quantity hedges (fail) and provenance hedges (pass only inside informationReceiptPools.js). Acceptance U3 (the ration is a PER-VARIANT NET TEST at the point of edit, not a per-file aggregate checked afterwards — four additions slipped a sample written to demonstrate the rule) and U8 (before cutting a rationed adverb, check whether a sibling pool exists that the adverb distinguishes the variant from).

rules.statement: In the Herald, a line meant to move is earned by a plain fact stated in the sentence before it, and it fires in a minority of entries. No entry closes on a moral, a summary, an aphorism or an uplift. The crier may hold one such line; the receipt pools ordinarily hold none.
rules.figure: R5 abstract-noun closer 0.020 (PROBE_ALL §6: 0.35× the 0.057 median) and the `came to nothing` family at 8 of 373 (2.1%, §4's tic table) — the estate's nearest measurable proxy for an uplift or anti-climax close. DIRECTION: hold both. SIZE: R5 abstract closer held at ≤0.030 and the uplift-closer family held at ≤0.02 while the moving line is admitted. THE MOVING LINE'S OWN RATE IS NOT MEASURED; kay:38 sets no rate and the census is owed — this rule is a direction with no number and says so.
rules.faultGuard: Fault 6 (the evaluative close, 6 documents STRONG), named by kay:38 itself — the earned line becoming a per-entry slot is the closing-uplift metronome. GUARDS: K 38's own 'most Herald entries should contain no such line'; K 26's bar on the general aphorism, walkable (does the sentence name a thing in this world, or does it name life?); A9's — a gnomic closer is never CREATED where the BEFORE had none.
rules.grammar: A rationed optional move at the tail of a crier line only, licensed by the fact stated in the move before it (kay:38's earning condition expressed as a grammar dependency): the MOVING move may not be first, and may not follow another MOVING move in the same pool.
obeys: (3) a rationed move whose firing is seeded is the definition of a latent grammar; fired per entry it is the visible template the owner's directive names.
(7) product scope — a moving line about the world, never about a named character's fate.
(1) allocate — Kay alone carries the mechanism, with two SINGLE-source corroborations named as single rather than averaged in.
rules.test: A walker counting the moving-line move per register and failing on any run of two, plus kay:26's generalisation test run over R5's closers. Acceptance U9's second limb (the gnomic closer is ruled three ways across five items and needs its own explicit rule — this is that rule) and U5 (assert delivery, never citation).

rules.statement: In the Herald, record a civic event where it strikes — on a household, a trade or an office the engine holds as a standing civic fact — and put the cost in a DIFFERENT sentence, a later receipt, or nowhere. Some bills go unnamed. The household is never followed to an outcome.
rules.figure: R3 triad-list rate 0.012 (0.44× the 0.027 median) — HELD at ≤0.020, because martin:38's own named risk is that cause-effect-effect at fixed length is a tricolon in disguise. R3 pronoun closer 0.0769 (fingerprint) against martin-chronicle 0.054 and the bible 0.015 → DOWN to ≤0.055, a cut of 0.022, anchored on Martin's chronicle, the exemplar column that argues by concrete civic nouns. BOTH ARE R3 AND ARE DEFERRED TO HP-2's SIGNATURE. B0.3's caveat binds: name the referent at the close ONLY where the referent is a civic thing — the illustration refuter proved the rule does not reach an abstraction (ill-1 bought an echo for nothing).
rules.faultGuard: Fault 3 (the great-against-small pairing as a metronome if every entry ends on its small counterweight — kay:14 names it), fault 1 (hobb:8's 'a levy is a daughter's dowry deferred' as a stamped equation appended to every entry), fault 4 (kay:7 and hobb:8's tricolon of consequences). GUARDS: K 16's — put the bill in a different sentence, a later block or a parenthesis, and let some bills be recoverable only elsewhere; H 9's — persistence is shown by a NEW FACT, never by re-narrating; K 7's — two trades or four, never habitually three; M 38's — vary how far a consequence runs, and some stop at one.
rules.grammar: The BILL move, licensed by event provenance AND an institution row (HP-6). Order constraint, the rule's teeth: BILL MAY NOT IMMEDIATELY FOLLOW DEED IN THE SAME SENTENCE — that adjacency is the stamped equation. R-DST-B: this move exists in the Herald and nowhere else in the estate, because only here does a provenance field exist.
obeys: (7) THE PROMISE and product scope — kay:14's own guard, that the household is a STANDING CIVIC FACT never followed to an outcome, is the fate law stated by an exemplar; and hobb:8's own line, the household persists and the person is a role in it, keeps a NAMED character's fate out.
(5) the household and the office must be world-held rows, or HP-6 refuses the line.
(2) hobb:8 at 10 sources is why this rule exists at all, and why it lives here rather than in R1.
rules.test: A walker over the R3 homes counting DEED→BILL adjacency, consequence-chain length distribution and the pronoun-closer rate; plus check-pair.mjs's existing PRONOUN CLOSER ADDED arm, which needs only the Herald corpus. Acceptance U12 (R-DST-B) and U5 (the close-on-a-thing rule must be delivered, not cited).

rules.statement: In the Herald's causal grammar and join molds (R4), keep every mold family populated across all four argument forms (N / F / V / A), let no composed chain use one connective pool twice, and measure R4's spread INSIDE the estate — never against an exemplar column, because R4 is a phrase register.
rules.figure: R4 pronoun closer 0.128 (PROBE_ALL §6: 2.56× the 0.050 median) — the join molds land on 'it', and a mold's closer becomes the composed chain's closer → DOWN to ≤0.077, a cut of 0.051, anchored on R3's OWN figure and deliberately not on an exemplar column per [R-12] (R4 is a phrase register scored on sentence metrics, so exemplar comparison is invalid). R4 mean within-pool word sd 0.6, the estate's lowest → UP to ≥1.0, still the estate's low end (R5 is 1.3), because a four-to-seven-word phrase cannot carry more without becoming a clause.
rules.faultGuard: Fault 9 at the connective level — sixteen connective pools and two terminals, and if one dominates every composed chain reads the same (R4's top gram `and the` is 14 of 133, 10.5%) — plus fault 17. GUARDS: [R-12]'s caveat made a RULE (never compare a phrase register to a prose column); hobb:32's — term consistency requires the WORD to repeat while the FACT must not, and the engine must tell them apart or it will suppress the wrong repetition; hobb:32's inverse risk, the thesaurus in reverse, which bars curing a dominant connective by minting an uncommon one.
rules.grammar: This IS the grammar's connective layer: eight typed edges (§0c) × sixteen connective pools × the four argument forms. The closed set of orders draws its joints from here, and the order constraint is that no chain repeats a connective pool. The F/N split — named by the inventory the load-bearing rule of the whole section — is not touched.
obeys: (3) B-GRAMMAR's substrate — a closed set of orders needs a populated joint vocabulary, or the 'variation' is one connective wearing five orders.
(6) B-CLAIM — a connective is word order, which is spendable; the edge TYPE is a claim, which is not.
(2) kay:44 at 8 sources supplies the distribution law this rule is an instance of.
rules.test: A walker over heraldCausalGrammar.js and heraldJoinMolds.js counting per-family argument-form occupancy, per-chain connective reuse and the closer distribution; the avalanche32(fnv1a32(seed)) selection must be re-derived because FNV-1a's low bit is a parity and a raw % 8 on a power-of-two pool leaves half the pool unreachable (PROSE_INVENTORY §7.4, measured). Acceptance U10 (measured against the pool's other variants) and U4 (count the SHAPE, not the phrase — a connective swapped for a synonym moves the column without moving the failure).

rules.statement: In the Herald's disclosure and lifecycle family (R4b), write an absence in the clerk's third person, and only where the simulation knows why the gap exists. No frame gram appears in more than one line in ten of the family. Some events fire no disclosure at all.
rules.figure: R4b colon rate 0.280 — 3.54× the 0.079 median (PROBE_ALL §6) — which is the `traces back to one thing: {cause}` frame measured → DOWN to ≤0.150, a cut of 0.13 (roughly half the family losing the colon frame; the exemplar colon range is 0.000-0.125 and tolkien-elevated's 0.125 is the ceiling I stop just above, because a disclosure line has a real use for a colon a narrative sentence does not). R4b `the compromise` 8 of 50 (16.0%, lift 448) → ≤5 of 50 (0.16 → ≤0.10). HELD: R4b pools-uniform-in-segment-count 0.455, the best figure in the whole Herald and better than the corpus median — it must not regress while the frames are spread.
rules.faultGuard: Fault 5 in its lacunae form — dnd:23's own warning about a disclosure repeated across a dossier, and hobb:19's 'a metronome of lacunae'. GUARDS: kay:11's — the four forms are a pool with long gaps and some entries fire none; hobb:19's — the gap must correlate with something the simulation knows (a fire, a bad year, a change of office), so an absence is a CONSEQUENCE OF WORLD STATE, never a decoration; leguin:4's — the gap is in the RECORD, never in the world, which keeps a disclosure from becoming an assertion that a thing did not happen.
rules.grammar: The WITHHOLD move, R4b only, licensed by an absence the simulation can name. Grammar G5 (DEED → WITHHOLD) is the only order it enters, and its firing is seeded with a long gap rather than per-event.
obeys: (4) EVERY DOSSIER ELEMENT GETS THE FULL FORM, in the one place in this register where the absence is WRITTEN rather than omitted — and full form is not full content, so a disclosure names a gap the world holds and never manufactures one.
(5) an absence the simulation cannot name is a fact bought for an effect, in the negative.
(3) the four forms are a seeded draw, never a rotation.
rules.test: A walker over heraldIntegrity.js DISCLOSURE_LINES, causeLifecycleVocabulary.js and causeWalk.js counting per-gram share, colon rate and inter-firing gap, plus a check that every disclosure resolves to a world-state cause. Acceptance U9 (a 'That is / This is' second sentence carrying the pool key's discriminating claim is not a gloss — a disclosure line is exactly that shape and must not be cut as one) and U12.

rules.statement: The Herald carries no question, no digit, no em dash and no exclamation. Retire the crier's two interrogatives — the estate's only diegetic questions — by rewriting each to its declarative claim, and cut the crier's exogenous AI-lexicon tells to the corpus median.
rules.figure: R5 question rate 0.005 — PROBE_ALL §6 grades it ∞ against a corpus median of 0 — which on 396 segments is EXACTLY 2 SEGMENTS → 0 (an exact zero is correct because it is a binary law, not a distribution: the estate has 0 questions in R1, R2, R3, R4, R4b, R6, R17, A-U and A-W). R5 AI-tells/variant EXOGENOUS 0.024, 3× the 0.008 median and the corpus's highest, which on 373 variants is 9 variants → ≤0.008, i.e. ≤3. Note: R5 is the ONE register whose raw and exogenous tell rates are identical at 0.024 — none of the crier's tells is product vocabulary, so none is excusable as the lexicon.
rules.faultGuard: Fault 19 in reverse — the lexicon swap as a false cure, which is the owner's own ruling ('AI prose with better vocabulary'). GUARD: own row 50 shows the LEXICAL half of the catalogue already cleared at 0.004 exogenous in R1 and R3 and states plainly that the STRUCTURAL half (faults 5, 9, 15) is where the estate still resembles the machine — so this rule is explicitly a MECHANICAL TIDY, NOT A CURE, and must not be reported as one. best-ai.md's closing note settles it: the discriminating signal is structural (93.2% macro-F1 from narrative features alone), so a de-slopping pass on vocabulary leaves it untouched.
rules.grammar: none — a mechanical prohibition on a character class and a word list, at the lexeme level, below the grammar.
obeys: (7) the standing laws directly — no digits in prose, and B0.8's four absolutes kept on purpose.
(2) graded on 18 documents and reported as mechanical, not as taste.
(6) B-CLAIM — a lexeme is spendable, but the two questions are the exception: a question is a MODALITY, so each must be rewritten to its declarative claim, never merely deleted.
rules.test: check-pair.mjs's existing DIGIT / EM DASH / EXCLAMATION arms plus a new question arm, run over a Herald corpus; PROBE_ALL's metrics.mjs AI-tell counter re-run on newsVoice.js with the exogenous filter. Acceptance U11 (digit-free is not band-clean — the count and duration vocabularies checked in the same pass) and U4 (count the shape, not the phrase).

refusedTechniques.name: Kay's prolepsis and the told outcome (kay:6, S3; §3.2 leaves the CHRONICLE open)
refusedTechniques.why: THE PROMISE makes lived history immutable and a seed a starting world forever; A2 makes a bare future indicative a FATE breach ANYWHERE, and check-pair.mjs's FUTURE INDICATIVE ADDED arm already exists for exactly this. §3.2 is open for the chronicle line only, and the Herald is not the chronicle. Kay's own bound — at most one clause — is not offered here.

refusedTechniques.name: Hobb's saying-from-a-closed-pool as a Herald OPENER (hobb:21, SINGLE, graded PARTIAL by its own file)
refusedTechniques.why: Refused as an opener; admitted only under HP-6's licensing. Its own conflict field is the reason: an unexplained saying that carries load becomes the block's thesis (against hobb:7), and the DEITY DOCTRINE requires a saying to stay a CUSTOM OF THE PLACE and never a doctrine the record endorses. martin:40's transmission form — the record shows a saying passing from mouth to mouth rather than asserting it exists — is the licensed shape, and it needs a saying row the world holds.

refusedTechniques.name: Tolkien's alliterative prose and the elevated register (tolkien:B2's alliteration limb; tolkien:A1-A3, C4)
refusedTechniques.why: tolkien:B2's own gate is that alliteration crosses into prose ONLY where a people's verse has just been heard, and that trigger does not exist in the product; B2 is graded PARTIAL for this reason and its tripling is dropped rather than templated. Positively: dnd:5 makes the Herald the PLAINER register by design, and §3.5's antique-air conflict is unsettled with three verified mechanisms for one permission — a register with no need of the permission does not adjudicate it.

refusedTechniques.name: Wolfe's unreliable record (wolfe:13b) as a property of the receipt itself
refusedTechniques.why: §3.14 is SETTLED as a PRODUCT LAW, never as a Wolfe claim: the dossier is the ground truth the game state reconciles against, so a receipt that lies breaks the save contract, not merely the voice. wolfe:14 (SINGLE) IS admitted as the escape valve — a voice quoted inside the record may lie and the record does not say so — with W 14's own guard that a tag ('he claimed', 'so he said') destroys it, which is HP-7's no-hedge rule from the other side.

refusedTechniques.name: Martin's dialogue engine (§3.1, SETTLED)
refusedTechniques.why: Dialogue is measured at 0.000 in the crier and the ladder and 0.0003 in dossier-state (own row 52; fault 13 'cleared by absence'). Speech survives only mediated (martin:4), as a saying (kay:39), or as an untagged quoted voice (wolfe:20 — HP-4). Two speakers explaining the world to each other is fault 13's canonical form, and wolfe:21's own file names its author doing it.

refusedTechniques.name: The moving or evaluative line as a per-entry SLOT (kay:38 applied per entry; kay:26's aphorism; A9's created gnomic closer)
refusedTechniques.why: Refused as a slot, admitted rationed at HP-8. kay:38's own guard is the refusal — most Herald entries should contain no such line — and A9 bars CREATING a gnomic closer where the BEFORE had none. Fault 6 (6 documents) is the shape it becomes.

refusedTechniques.name: The exemplars' punctuation freedoms (B0.8): em dashes, questions, exclamations, digits
refusedTechniques.why: Kept at zero ON PURPOSE by the voice bible and ruling (7); every exemplar column breaches at least one. R5's two questions (0.005 on 396 segments) are the estate's only diegetic breach and HP-12 retires them. NEAR-REFUSAL RECORDED: dnd:27's person-of-record minimum (6 sources) is admitted because a receipt names people, but its own HIGH anti-AI grade is carried — three-beat person lines across many residents is the purest metronome in the design — and its full form is owner question Q7, which this reconciliation does not answer.

conflicts: PARATAXIS AT THE EVENT (§3.4, OPEN). FOR: tolkien:A4 (6 — clauses chained with 'and', the causal connective withheld at the event; Bolding 663's cultural split), kay:25 (1, the polysyndetic chain reserved for loss), leguin:39 (1). AGAINST: hobb:15 (3, Oliver alone on the breach limb — extensive parataxis marks the moment the record voice BREAKS). Both verified. The Herald is one of the two registers where the conflict is live, and HP-10 deliberately does NOT decide it: it constrains spread only. Our own figures say we have neither device today (R3 semicolon 0.136, R5 0.198, R3 triad 0.012). Q10 is the owner's.

WHETHER A CRIER LINE MAY CARRY WOLFE'S EXAMINATION FORM (§3.1's one open limb). FOR: wolfe:21 (3, 'the form is admitted, the exposition is not'; Registers: H primary) and leguin:41 (1, a line that expects an answer — the Herald is the one product surface that addresses somebody). AGAINST: fault 13 at 14 documents — the line that ends on a hook, and dialogue that states what the speaker wants. They do not settle each other because they address different halves: leguin:41 licenses ADDRESS, fault 13 bars the HOOK, and no evidence says whether an addressed line can be held short of a hook by a pool. The count is also lopsided the wrong way: 1 and 3 sources for the permission against 14 documents for the fault.

THE MOVING LINE'S RATE (kay:38's own boundary). kay:38 states that the boundary between the Herald and the archivist RESTS ENTIRELY on this technique being rationed, and gives no rate; the estate measures no proxy for it. HP-8 therefore sets a direction with no number — a rule with a hole in it, recorded as such rather than filled by invention.

WHICH LENGTH LAW GOVERNS THE CRIER. dnd:40 (7) reads 'one or two brief sentences, rarely three, never past four'; the annex's own HEADLINE definition (RECEIPT_POOLS_CAUSAL.md §0a) reads one sentence with multi-link chains FORBIDDEN. R3 keeps the annex law (1.170 segments a variant). R5's measured shape (1.062 segments, p50 18 words — 2.25× the corpus median) is a LONG SINGLE SENTENCE, which neither law describes well.
